paper.title_en: Probing dense QCD with gauge/gravity duality
paper.abstract_en: The study of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at finite density remains one of the most formidable frontiers in the physics of strong interactions. QCD is strongly coupled at intermediate temperatures and densities, rendering perturbative techniques ineffective. Furthermore, first-principles calculations via lattice QCD, which have been highly successful at low densities, are fundamentally hindered by the numerical sign problem when describing dense matter. This leaves the properties of dense QCD matter, such as that produced in heavy-ion collisions or found in neutron stars, difficult to determine with conventional methods.Our research addresses these environments by utilizing the holographic principle, specifically the gauge/gravity duality, to investigate the strongly coupled dynamics of QCD. Originally developed in the context of string theory, the gauge/gravity duality, with the AdS/CFT correspondence as its canonical example, provides a dictionary that relates strongly coupled quantum field theories to gravitational theories in a higher-dimensional spacetime. The quantum field theory, which in our case models QCD, lives on the boundary of this spacetime. Within this framework, complicated problems regarding thermodynamic properties are translated into soluble geometric problems in the gravitational theory. In particular, we use black hole solutions of classical gravity to model the quark-gluon plasma. A central component of this work involves the development and refinement of bottom-up holographic models, which are phenomenologically constructed and tuned to reproduce key features of the boundary theory. Specifically, we focus on models based on the Einstein--Maxwell-dilaton and Dirac--Born--Infeld actions. These models are fitted to lattice QCD data at zero density and are then used to infer properties of QCD matter at finite density. Beyond investigating the transition between hadronic matter and the quark-gluon plasma, we also explore the potential for exotic states of matter that may emerge at finite density. This includes Higgs phases motivated by color superconductivity and spatially modulated inhomogeneous phases.The research offers model-based predictions for the location of the QCD critical point, where the line of first-order phase transitions terminates. We discuss our results in light of data from the Beam Energy Scan II program at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. Furthermore, our findings suggest that dense matter near the critical point may not be homogeneous, but may instead exhibit spatial modulation, in a region of the phase diagram close to that probed experimentally. We also provide an example of how critical behavior depends on the flavor structure of the theory, and find that this behavior may be suppressed by the constraints on flavor composition present in heavy-ion collisions. These results provide new insights into the phase structure of dense QCD matter.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该论文用规范/引力对偶（含AdS/CFT）构建自下而上的全息模型（Einstein–Maxwell-dilaton与Dirac–Born–Infeld作用量），用零密度格点QCD数据拟合后外推到有限密度，讨论QCD临界点、空间调制非均匀相与Higgs相等问题，并与RHIC束流能量扫描II数据对照。理论框架具体、方法链条清晰、结论基于模型预测且如实标注不确定性，与全息凝聚态/强耦合物质主题高度相关，值得点击进一步阅读。
decision.title_zh: 用规范/引力对偶探测稠密QCD
decision.abstract_zh: 在有限密度下研究量子色动力学（QCD）仍然是强相互作用物理中最艰巨的前沿之一。QCD在中等温度和密度下处于强耦合，使微扰技术失效。此外，通过格点QCD进行的第一性原理计算在低密度下非常成功，但在描述稠密物质时从根本上受到数值符号问题的阻碍。这使得稠密QCD物质的性质——例如重离子碰撞中产生的物质或中子星中的物质——难以用常规方法确定。我们的研究利用全息原理，特别是规范/引力对偶，来研究QCD的强耦合动力学，以此应对这些环境。规范/引力对偶最初是在弦论背景下发展起来的，以AdS/CFT对应为其典范例子，它提供了一本字典，将强耦合量子场论与高维时空中的引力理论联系起来。量子场论（在我们的情形中用于模拟QCD）生活在该时空的边界上。在此框架内，关于热力学性质的复杂问题被转化为引力理论中可解的几何问题。特别地，我们使用经典引力的黑洞解来模拟夸克-胶子等离子体。本工作的一个核心组成部分是发展和改进自下而上的全息模型，这些模型是现象学地构造的，并被调节以重现边界理论的关键特征。具体而言，我们关注基于Einstein--Maxwell-dilaton和Dirac--Born--Infeld作用量的模型。这些模型在零密度下拟合格点QCD数据，然后被用来推断有限密度下QCD物质的性质。除了研究强子物质与夸克-胶子等离子体之间的转变之外，我们还探索了在有限密度下可能出现的奇异物质态的潜力。这包括由色超导性所激发的Higgs相以及空间调制的非均匀相。该研究给出了关于QCD临界点位置——即一阶相变线的终点——的基于模型的预测。我们结合相对论重离子对撞机Beam Energy Scan II计划的数据讨论我们的结果。此外，我们的发现表明，临界点附近的稠密物质可能不是均匀的，而可能表现出空间调制，且位于相图中接近实验所探测区域的区域。我们还提供了一个例子，说明临界行为如何依赖于理论的味结构，并发现这种行为可能被重离子碰撞中对味组成的限制所抑制。这些结果为稠密QCD物质的相结构提供了新的见解。
